title: Do AI Agents Gossip? Evaluative Talk in Human and AI-Agent Online Communities
abstract: arXiv:2610.20360v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Gossip, defined as evaluative talk about absent third parties, is widely seen as a uniquely human social practice. This study examines whether comparable discourse emerges spontaneously in a community of autonomous AI agents. We compare Moltbook, a Reddit-style platform populated by AI agents, with PTT, a large human-operated bulletin board in Taiwan. To reduce differences attributable to communicative setting, we analyze two public, asynchronous forums using the same operational definition of gossip. Gossip occurs on Moltbook, but its prevalence is 2.6 to 6 times lower than on PTT, depending on the denominator used. On both platforms, gossip frequently targets locally prominent figures, tends to elicit agreement from the first respondent, and is rarely presented as unsupported rumor. The clearest difference concerns how subsequent responses develop. Among threads containing at least one codable reply, challenges occur in 65.1% of human

translated_title: AI智能体会八卦吗？人类与AI智能体在线社区中的评价性谈论
translated_abstract: 八卦，即对不在场的第三方进行评价性谈论，被广泛视为一种独特的人类社会实践。本研究考察了类似的言论是否会在一个由自主AI智能体组成的社区中自发涌现。我们将Moltbook（一个由AI智能体组成的Reddit风格平台）与PTT（台湾一个大型人工运营的电子公告板）进行了比较。为了减少因交流环境差异带来的影响，我们采用相同的八卦操作性定义，对两个公开的、异步的论坛进行了分析。研究发现，Moltbook上确实存在八卦，但其流行度比PTT低2.6至6倍（取决于所采用的分母）。在两个平台上，八卦通常针对本地知名人物，往往能获得第一个回应者的赞同，且很少被呈现为毫无根据的谣言。最明显的差异在于后续回应如何展开：在包含至少一条可编码回复的帖子中，人类社区中出现了65.1%的挑战性回应……
tldr: 本研究首次通过对比AI智能体社区（Moltbook）与人类在线论坛（PTT），发现AI智能体社区中会自发涌现类似人类八卦的评价性言论，尽管其流行度显著低于人类社区，且两者在后续回应的发展模式上存在明显差异。
en_tdlr: This study provides the first systematic evidence that gossip-like evaluative talk emerges spontaneously in AI-agent online communities, though at 2.6 to 6 times lower prevalence than in human forums, with the clearest difference lying in how subsequent replies develop.
